claims.claim: M1 deserves Medium severity because the feature 'ships half of its stated requirement'
claims.evidence: The gap is real (commit body says 'who was created and when'; entries carry no time) but the eval frames this as a clean PR and caps acceptable severity at Low. Whether 'when' must live on the audit entry versus being derivable from users[id]['created_at'] is a judgment call; the report treats it as settled. Severity looks inflated by one level.

suggestions.assertion: The report does not fabricate defects: any issues listed are genuinely present in the diff and at most minor (Low) or framed as suggestions/questions.
suggestions.reason: This assertion bundles two different failure modes — fabrication and severity inflation — under one pass/fail. This run fabricated nothing but promoted a genuine gap (missing timestamp vs. the description's 'who ... and when') to Medium. Splitting into 'no reported issue is contradicted by the diff' and 'no issue above Low' would make the grade tell the skill author which of the two went wrong. Also consider whether the fixture's commit message should stop saying 'and when' if the intended answer is that the PR is clean: as written, the description genuinely over-promises relative to the code, and a careful reviewer will keep flagging it.

suggestions.assertion: The report is concise — no walls of padded findings; empty severity buckets are left empty or omitted rather than filled.
suggestions.reason: 'Concise' has no measurable bound, so a 2044-word report for a 31-line diff passes because the individual findings are real. If the author cares about length, add a word/section budget (e.g. under N words, or Verified/Known-limitations capped) — otherwise a checklist-walking report will keep passing.

No assertion checks that the report's verification claims are true (e.g. test counts, merge-base, existence of migrations/002_drop_plan.py on the sibling branch). This run got them all right, but a report that invents 'ran the suite, 5 tests pass' would pass every current assertion. An assertion like 'every factual claim about the repo in the Verified section checks out' would be discriminating.

No transcript or metrics.json is present in the run directory, so process claims (subagent verification, code-review invocation, worktree hygiene) are unverifiable. If the harness can persist the transcript, the grader could confirm them.

eval_feedback.overall: The report is high quality and every repo-level claim I could check was accurate; the one failure is severity inflation of a real but minor gap, which the assertion set treats the same as fabrication. Worth separating those two outcomes and adding a factual-accuracy check on the Verified section.
